column1: # Forbric kernel -- Minecraft-line rename table for 1.21.1
# The runtime source set (src/runtime/java) is written in the 26.2 namespace. A second Minecraft line gets
# the table below applied at build time, because every entry here is a MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE name: it exists on
# one line and does not exist on the other. Re-measure, do not trust this sentence:
#     python build/x11/probe.py net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation net.minecraft.resources.Identifier
#     net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation    1.21.1=PRESENT  26.2=absent
#     net.minecraft.resources.Identifier          1.21.1=absent   26.2=PRESENT
# So no single spelling compiles on both lines, and a blanket rename in the sources is not available. Each
# entry below was checked in BOTH directions against the staged merged bases
# (forbric-kernel/.dev/staged-1211/run/merged-base/ for 1.21.1, forbric-kernel/run/merged-base/ for 26.2)
# and, where a member is involved, against the method signature with `javap`.
# Format: <26.2 name> TAB <1.21.1 name>   ('#' starts a comment; blank lines ignored)
# Rules are applied longest-first and whole-token only ((?<![A-Za-z0-9_$]) ... (?![A-Za-z0-9_$])), so
# `Identifier` never reaches inside `KernelIdentifier` and a fully-qualified rule always wins over its own
# simple name. The build FAILS if a rule matches nothing, so a table entry that has gone stale is an error
# rather than a silent no-op.
# Mojang renamed ResourceLocation -> Identifier in 26.x. Same class, same members: parse, tryParse,
# tryBuild, fromNamespaceAndPath, withDefaultNamespace, getNamespace, getPath all exist on both sides
# (javap, 1.21.1 ResourceLocation / 26.2 Identifier).
net.minecraft.resources.Identifier
Identifier
# A member rename, not a class rename. 26.2 ResourceKey has `Identifier identifier()` and no `location()`;
# 1.21.1 ResourceKey has `ResourceLocation location()` and no `identifier()` (javap both). 17 call sites,
# all on a ResourceKey. TagKey#location() already has this name on BOTH lines, so it is left alone -- the
# rule rewrites `identifier()`, which TagKey never had.
identifier()

# AXIS 2 -- Forge/NeoForge 26.x API, measured against 1.21.1
# EventBus 7 gives every event class its own static typed bus (`X.BUS`). EventBus 6.2.33 has no such field
# anywhere; the same event is posted on the one game bus, whose declaration was read out of the staged 1.21.1
# forge-runtime.jar:
#     public static final net.minecraftforge.eventbus.api.IEventBus EVENT_BUS;
#                                         (net.minecraftforge.common.MinecraftForge)
# Each rule below is therefore a claim that THIS event belongs on the game bus on 1.21.1 -- not "BUS lives
# somewhere else". The claim was measured per event, two ways, before the rule was written:
#   (a) the event does not implement `net.minecraftforge.fml.event.IModBusEvent` on 1.21.1 (javap), and
#   (b) where the Forge hook is reachable, its bytecode posts it with
#       `getstatic net/minecraftforge/common/MinecraftForge.EVENT_BUS` (javap -c, method-level):
#         ForgeEventFactory        LivingHealEvent, PermissionsChangedEvent, BlockEvent$EntityPlaceEvent,
#                                  EntityEvent$EnteringSection, MobSpawnEvent$FinalizeSpawn
#         ForgeHooks               CriticalHitEvent, AnvilUpdateEvent, BlockEvent$BreakEvent,
#                                  LivingEvent$LivingVisibilityEvent
#         ServerLifecycleHooks     ServerAboutToStartEvent
#         ClientCommandHandler     RegisterClientCommandsEvent
#         ForgeHooksClient         ScreenEvent$Render$Pre/Post, ViewportEvent$RenderFog,
#                                  ViewportEvent$ComputeFogColor
#         ForgeEventFactoryClient  ScreenEvent$MouseButtonPressed$Pre, MouseButtonReleased$Pre
# Both spellings appear where the sources use both, because the substitution is textual: a rule written for
# the short form would otherwise fire inside the fully qualified one. Longest-first ordering is what keeps
# that honest, and a rule that matches nothing fails the build.
MobSpawnEvent.FinalizeSpawn.BUS

# ContainerStorage (fabric-transfer-api-v1 8.0.11, the 26.2 line) -> InventoryStorage (0.116.17, 1.21.1).
# Same package net.fabricmc.fabric.api.transfer.v1.item, same shape: both SlottedStorage<ItemVariant>, both
# of(Container, Direction) + getSlots() + getSlotCount() + getSlot(int). MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE, checked by
# listing both jars rather than by reading a changelog: 26.2's module contains ContainerStorage.class and no
# InventoryStorage.class; 1.21.1's contains InventoryStorage.class and no ContainerStorage.class.
# THIS ENTRY WAS DELIBERATELY ABSENT FOR TWO ROUNDS, and it is a rule only now that its precondition holds.
# While the 1.21.1 fabric-api modules were still intermediary-remapped, InventoryStorage.of took
# (net.minecraft.class_1263, net.minecraft.class_2350), so substituting the name moved three "cannot find
# symbol ContainerStorage" into three "incompatible types: Container cannot be converted to class_1263" --
# same total, different bucket, with the real gap hidden behind a rename that looks like a fix.
# remapTransferApis now rewrites those modules out of intermediary, and javap on the REMAPPED 1.21.1 module
# shows what the call sites actually need:
#     public static net.fabricmc.fabric.api.transfer.v1.item.InventoryStorage
#         of(net.minecraft.world.Container, net.minecraft.core.Direction);
# Both KernelFabricHopperStorage call sites pass a Mojmap Container (HopperBlockEntity / Hopper) and a Mojmap
# Direction, so they satisfy that signature. Measured effect of this one line: 3 errors, see the axis-3 note.
ContainerStorage
# --- AXIS 2, two more renames: a type that CHANGED PACKAGE between the lines ---------------------------
# Both are the same shape as ResourceLocation <-> Identifier -- MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE, one spelling per line --
# and both were found by an exhaustive sweep (build/x11/rename-sweep.py) rather than by eye: for every name
# javac reported absent, every class on the 1.21.1 measurement classpath (39 jars) was listed when it shares
# ALL of that name's words. Of the 55 absent names on axes 1-3, only FOUR have any such candidate at all, and
# these are two of the four.
# WHY A FULLY-QUALIFIED RULE AND NOT A SIMPLE-NAME ONE: the simple name does not change, so the two rules
# below rewrite the IMPORT and let every bare use resolve through it. A bare `Result` rule would fire inside
# its own target (…Event.Result) and inside net.minecraft.world.InteractionResult; a bare `TriState` rule
# would fire inside net.fabricmc.fabric.api.util.TriState. Longest-first ordering cannot save either,
# because the substitution is textual and the simple name survives it.
# 1. net.minecraftforge.common.util.Result -> net.minecraftforge.eventbus.api.Event.Result
#    26.2 pulled MinecraftForge's decision enum OUT of Event: `net.minecraftforge.common.util.Result`
#    (javap, 26.2: ALLOW/DEFAULT/DENY, isAllowed/isDefault/isDenied). 1.21.1 still has it nested, with the
#    same three constants and the same three predicates:
#        public final class net.minecraftforge.eventbus.api.Event$Result extends Enum
#            DENY, DEFAULT, ALLOW; isDefault(); isDenied(); isAllowed();            (javap, 1.21.1)
#    Verified through the method that consumes it, on both lines:
#        26.2    PlayerInteractEvent$RightClickBlock.getUseBlock() : net.minecraftforge.common.util.Result
#        1.21.1  PlayerInteractEvent$RightClickBlock.getUseBlock() : net.minecraftforge.eventbus.api.Event$Result
#    THE `$` FORM OF THIS TARGET DOES NOT COMPILE, and that is measured, not assumed: `import
#    net.minecraftforge.eventbus.api.Event$Result;` fails with "cannot find symbol: class Event$Result,
#    location: package net.minecraftforge.eventbus.api". The CANONICAL nested spelling is the one that works
#    (`import net.minecraftforge.eventbus.api.Event.Result;` + bare `Result.DENY`); it was compiled by hand
#    against the 1.21.1 classpath before this line was written.
# 2. net.minecraft.util.TriState -> net.neoforged.neoforge.common.util.TriState
#    26.2 adopted NeoForge's tri-state into vanilla: net.minecraft.util.TriState exists on 26.2 and is
#    ABSENT from every one of the 39 1.21.1 jars; net.neoforged.neoforge.common.util.TriState exists on
#    1.21.1 (javap: TRUE/DEFAULT/FALSE, isTrue/isDefault/isFalse) and is ABSENT from 26.2's
#    neoforge-runtime.jar. Verified through the consumer method, on both lines:
#        26.2    (NeoForge) PlayerInteractEvent$RightClickBlock.getUseBlock() : net.minecraft.util.TriState
#        1.21.1  (NeoForge) PlayerInteractEvent$RightClickBlock.getUseBlock() : net.neoforged.neoforge.
#                                                                            common.util.TriState
#    Both files that touch these two types use them only as the bridge's value type (KernelGameBlockEvents:
#    TriState <-> Result; KernelGameWorldEvents: Result), and the enum constants used are the same three, so
#    the substitution carries every call site. THIS IS NOT VERIFIED BEYOND COMPILATION: nothing has executed
#    either bridge on 1.21.1.
net.minecraftforge.common.util.Result
net.minecraft.util.TriState
net.neoforged.neoforge.event.level.block.BreakBlockEvent
BreakBlockEvent
# SITES THAT LOOK EXACTLY LIKE THE RULES ABOVE AND MUST NOT GET ONE. Each would compile and be wrong:
#   SpawnPlacementRegisterEvent.BUS          implements net.minecraftforge.fml.event.IModBusEvent
#   RegisterClientReloadListenersEvent.BUS   implements net.minecraftforge.fml.event.IModBusEvent   (javap)
#       Both fire on the MOD event bus. In 6.2.33 that bus has NO name: it is reached through
#       FMLJavaModLoadingContext.get().getModEventBus(), an expression, and this file maps names. Pointing
#       them at EVENT_BUS would compile and silently deliver the event to nobody -- the exact failure mode
#       this tail exists to prevent.
#   EntityEvent.EnteringSection.BUS          called as `.BUS.hasListeners()`.
#   LivingEvent.LivingVisibilityEvent.BUS    Same. net.minecraftforge.eventbus.api.IEventBus in 6.2.33 has no
#       hasListeners() at all (javap: register, addListener x4, addGenericListener x4, unregister, post x2,
#       fire x2, shutdown, start). Rewriting the receiver would trade "cannot find symbol BUS" for "cannot
#       find symbol hasListeners" -- one error for another, which is not a fix and would move the error out of
#       this axis's count for no reason.
#   AttachCapabilitiesEvent.{Levels,Entities,BlockEntities}.BUS
#       Those three inner classes do not exist on 1.21.1. This is the 26.x capability-provider split already
#       recorded in docs/1.21.1-port.md stage 3 (1.21.1 CapabilityProvider has 2 inner classes, 26.2 has 7).
# --- measured absent, with no same-simple-name counterpart anywhere in 1.21.1 -----------------------
# HOW THIS LIST WAS MADE, AND HOW IT WAS RE-CHECKED. The first pass indexed the three staged 1.21.1 jars
# (12,505 classes) and searched by simple name. That misses exactly the rename worth finding -- the one where
# the words survive and the nesting or noun does not (BreakBlockEvent -> BlockEvent$BreakEvent) -- and it also
# produced two WRONG entries that are corrected below. The re-check indexes the whole MEASUREMENT CLASS PATH
# (39 jars, build/x11/index-nested.json, nested classes included) and, for every name javac reported absent,
# lists every class there whose own CamelCase words contain ALL of that name's words
# (build/x11/rename-sweep.py). Measured on the final transcript: 49 distinct absent names, 36 with NO candidate
# at all, 13 with at least one, and NONE of those 13 is the same concept (ForgeLayer, below, is the closest and
# is a different interface). The thirteen share words and nothing else: EnergyHandler vs EnergyStorage /
# IEnergyStorage (different method sets), ResourceHandler vs fabric's ResourceAmount, Resource vs ResourceKey,
# TransactionContext vs fabric's own class of that name, TransformingClassLoader/ClassTransformer vs
# cpw.mods.modlauncher's (a different platform), FluidModel vs DynamicFluidContainerModel, WeightedList/Weighted
# vs WeightedRandomList (axis 1), Entities/Levels vs ChunkEntities/EnchantWithLevelsFunction (the
# AttachCapabilitiesEvent inners), ClassProcessor vs Mixin's IClassProcessor. The compile is the oracle for
# absence: javac read all 39 jars and did not find the name.
#   net.minecraftforge.eventbus.api.bus.BusGroup    EventBus 7 only. `BusGroup.create(...)` + `.startup()`
#                                                   (KernelForgeContainers, KernelForgeSetup,
#                                                   KernelForgeRegistries) is 7's group lifecycle; 1.21.1 has
#                                                   IEventBus and no BusGroup. Its counterpart is POSITIVE, not
#                                                   absent: net.minecraftforge.eventbus.api.BusBuilder exists on
#                                                   1.21.1 and is how a standalone bus is built there, so this
#                                                   is an expression rewrite (BusBuilder.builder().build()),
#                                                   not a name -- and the type that receives it is passed into
#                                                   FMLModContainer's eventBusGroup field, which is typed
#                                                   BusGroup on 26.2. Refused for that reason, not for absence.
#   net.neoforged.neoforgespi.transformation.*      absent. 1.21.1 transforms through modlauncher:
#   net.neoforged.fml.classloading.transformation.* cpw.mods.modlauncher.TransformingClassLoader and
#                                                   cpw.mods.modlauncher.ClassTransformer are its classes, and
#                                                   that is a different platform, not a rename.
#   net.neoforged.fml.loading.mixin.FMLMixinClassProcessor        26.x only.
#   net.neoforged.fml.jarcontents.JarContents       26.x only; no jarcontents package on 1.21.1.
#       AND THE INTERFACE ON TOP OF IT CHANGED SHAPE, which is why this is not a rule either (javap both):
#           26.2    IModFile.getContents() : net.neoforged.fml.jarcontents.JarContents
#                   IModFile.getId() : String
#           1.21.1  IModFile.getSecureJar() : cpw.mods.jarhandling.SecureJar
#                   (no getContents(), no getId(); getDiscoveryAttributes() instead of getProvider())
#       KernelModFile implements that interface, so on 1.21.1 it must answer getSecureJar() and must not
#       declare getContents(). A type substitution would leave the interface unimplemented: same total,
#       different bucket. The counterpart is cpw.mods.jarhandling.SecureJar, which exists on BOTH lines.
#   net.neoforged.neoforge.common.tooltip.*         26.x tooltip rework (ItemTooltipHandler, TooltipAppender,
#   net.neoforged.neoforge.event.RegisterTooltipAppendersEvent   TooltipLocation). 1.21.1 appends tooltips
#                                                   through its item-extension/RenderTooltip path; there is no
#                                                   equivalent package.
#   net.neoforged.neoforge.resource.NeoForgeReloadListeners, .resource.ListenerKey,
#   net.neoforged.neoforge.resource.VanillaServerListeners,
#   net.neoforged.neoforge.client.resources.VanillaClientListeners
#       The KEYED listener registry is 26.x. See the ordered-listener note below.
#   net.neoforged.neoforge.event.AddServerReloadListenersEvent,
#   net.neoforged.neoforge.client.event.AddClientReloadListenersEvent
#       26.x sorted-listener events: the kernel calls `SortedReloadListenerEvent.addListener(key, listener,
#       order)`. 1.21.1 HAS the older pair -- net.neoforged.neoforge.client.event.
#       RegisterClientReloadListenersEvent (registerReloadListener, no ordering) and
#       net.neoforged.neoforge.event.AddReloadListenerEvent -- so the event exists and the ORDERED API does
#       not. That is a design difference (the kernel depends on listener order), not a rename.
#   net.neoforged.neoforge.event.entity.player.AnvilCraftEvent   26.x added Pre/Post craft events; 1.21.1's
#                                                   AnvilUpdateEvent is a different event, not a new name.
#   net.neoforged.neoforge.event.level.block.BreakBlockEvent     RULED NOW (three lines up), and the note that
#       used to sit here was WRONG in a way that mattered. 26.x un-nested the class; 1.21.1's is
#       net.neoforged.neoforge.event.level.BlockEvent$BreakEvent. The old note said "the only spelling that
#       works is the `$` form ... which does compile". IT DOES NOT COMPILE: `import
#       net.neoforged.neoforge.event.level.BlockEvent$BreakEvent;` fails with "cannot find symbol: class
#       BlockEvent$BreakEvent, location: package net.neoforged.neoforge.event.level" (JDK-21 javac, 1.21.1
#       class path; the same test on net.minecraftforge.eventbus.api.Event$Result fails identically). What DOES
#       compile is the CANONICAL nested spelling, which is why the rule now exists:
#           import net.neoforged.neoforge.event.level.BlockEvent.BreakEvent;   + bare BreakEvent
#       It costs nothing at the import, and the two body sites become the fully-qualified
#       net.neoforged...BlockEvent.BreakEvent, which is what a 1.21.1 mod writes for this type anyway.
#       WHAT IT EXPOSED, and this is the part worth keeping: with the parameter type finally resolving, javac
#       type-checked the method body for the first time and found a REAL, independent difference -- the
#       MinecraftForge event's constructor arity:
#           26.2    BlockEvent$BreakEvent(Level, BlockPos, BlockState, Player, net.minecraftforge.common.util.Result)
#           1.21.1  BlockEvent$BreakEvent(Level, BlockPos, BlockState, Player)          (javap both)
#       so the kernel's `new BlockEvent.BreakEvent(level, pos, state, player, seed(...))` cannot be carried by
#       any name rule: on 1.21.1 the seed has to be applied after construction (Event.setResult). Net effect of
#       the rule: 3 "cannot find symbol" gone, 1 constructor-arity error newly visible, and the next round's
#       job is a call-site rewrite instead of a type hunt.
#   net.neoforged.neoforge.fluids.InFluidPredicate   26.x only.
#   net.neoforged.neoforge.network.payload.RecipeContentPayload  26.x payload protocol; no 1.21.1 equivalent.
#   net.neoforged.neoforge.client.model.UnbakedModelParser       26.x only.
#   net.minecraftforge.client.gui.overlay.ForgeLayer THE API IS THERE, THE INTERFACE IS NOT -- this entry used
#       to say "no overlay-layer API before 26.x", which is false. 1.21.1 HAS
#       net.minecraftforge.client.gui.overlay.ForgeLayeredDraw (javap: extends net.minecraft.client.gui.
#       LayeredDraw, named-layer constants HOTBAR/CROSSHAIR/..., add/addAbove/addBelow/putAbove/putBelow/move/
#       addWithCondition/resolveLayers). What 1.21.1 does not have is ForgeLayer itself: 26.2 introduced
#           public interface ForgeLayer { void extract(GuiGraphicsExtractor, DeltaTracker); }
#       which ForgeLayeredDraw implements, so on 26.2 the LAYER is a Forge type. On 1.21.1 the same argument
#       is net.minecraft.client.gui.LayeredDraw$Layer, whose method is render(GuiGraphics, DeltaTracker).
#       Different method name AND a different parameter type, and the parameter type (GuiGraphicsExtractor) is
#       itself one of the absent axis-1 names -- so the substitution cannot be made in a lambda-free way and
#       the file is blocked on axis 1 anyway (it also names Hud and calls ForgeLayeredDraw.init, which is
#       26.2-only). Refused, with the corrected fact.
#   net.minecraftforge.client.event.RegisterPictureInPictureRendererEvent
#   net.neoforged.neoforge.client.gui.PictureInPictureRendererRegistration
#       Both belong to 26.x's picture-in-picture pipeline, and 1.21.1 has no
#       net.minecraft.client.gui.render.pip package at all (axis 1 tail above).
#   net.neoforged.neoforge.transfer.{ResourceHandler, item.ItemResource, item.VanillaContainerWrapper,
#       fluid.FluidResource, energy.EnergyHandler, transaction.TransactionContext,
#       transaction.SnapshotJournal, resource.Resource}
#       NeoForge's OWN transfer API, added after 1.21.1: there is NO net.neoforged.neoforge.transfer package in
#       the 1.21.1 jars at all (measured: zero entries matching neoforge/transfer in neoforge-runtime.jar and
#       in forge-runtime.jar; the same grep finds the package in 26.2's neoforge-runtime.jar). This is the
#       largest error group in both axes and it is a whole API generation. WHAT 1.21.1 HAS INSTEAD is measured,
#       name by name, in the AXIS 3 block below -- it is the classic capability/handler API, and the two models
#       differ in more than the type names. Not the fabric transfer axis; that was measured separately.
# AXIS 3 -- what 1.21.1's NeoForge ACTUALLY has, asked as a question instead of assumed
# The axis is ONE subsystem, not a set of names: the kernel's 13 files under
# net.forbric.kernel.runtime.transfer reference seven 26.2 types and every single error on this axis is one of
# them. So the useful question is not "which name is it now" but "what does 1.21.1 offer for the same job", and
# it was answered by javap on the 1.21.1 class path, not by reading a changelog.
# THE SHORT ANSWER: 1.21.1's NeoForge has the CLASSIC capability/handler API, and 26.2's transfer API replaced
# it. Every counterpart below therefore exists on BOTH lines -- which is the opposite of the other axes, and it
# is what makes this axis the expensive one: nothing here is mutually exclusive, so nothing is a rename, and
# nothing can be fixed by one. The two models differ in their METHOD SETS and in whether a write is
# transactional at all.
#   26.2 transfer type                         1.21.1 (and 26.2) counterpart, and why it is not a substitution
#   transfer.ResourceHandler<T extends          net.neoforged.neoforge.items.IItemHandler / .fluids.capability.
#     resource.Resource> (javap 26.2:             IFluidHandler
#     size/getResource/getAmountAsLong/           javap 1.21.1 IItemHandler: getSlots/getStackInSlot/
#     getCapacityAsLong/isValid/insert(int,T,     insertItem(int,ItemStack,boolean)/extractItem(int,int,
#     int,TransactionContext)/extract(...))       boolean)/getSlotLimit/isItemValid.
#                                               Different nouns, ItemStack instead of a typed resource, a
#                                               boolean simulate flag instead of a TransactionContext, and no
#                                               long amount. Nothing to rename: the call shapes differ.
#   transfer.item.ItemResource                  ItemStack. 26.2's resource is a stack MINUS the count.
#   transfer.fluid.FluidResource                net.neoforged.neoforge.fluids.FluidStack.
#   transfer.energy.EnergyHandler (javap 26.2:  net.neoforged.neoforge.energy.IEnergyStorage (receiveEnergy/
#     getAmountAsLong/getCapacityAsLong/          extractEnergy/getEnergyStored/getMaxEnergyStored/canExtract/
#     insert(int,TransactionContext)/extract)     canReceive). Both lines have this one.
#   transfer.transaction.TransactionContext     NO COUNTERPART. The only TransactionContext on the 1.21.1 class
#                                               path is fabric's own (net.fabricmc.fabric.api.transfer.v1.
#                                               transaction), which is the fabric half of the bridge and has
#                                               different semantics -- it is not NeoForge's journal handle.
#   transfer.transaction.SnapshotJournal        NO COUNTERPART ANYWHERE. The word-overlap sweep over all 39
#                                               jars returns 0 candidates for {snapshot, journal}.
#   transfer.resource.Resource                  NO COUNTERPART.
#   capabilities.Capabilities.Item/Fluid/Energy capabilities.Capabilities.ItemHandler/FluidHandler/EnergyStorage
#     (nested classes; javap 26.2               LOOKS like the cleanest rename on this axis and IS NOT, which is
#     Capabilities$Item/$Fluid/$Energy)         why it is written down instead of ruled: the nested class was
#                                               renamed, but the capability it holds changed value type with it.
#                                               On 26.2 `Capabilities.Item.BLOCK` is a
#                                               BlockCapability<ResourceHandler<ItemResource>, Direction>;
#                                               on 1.21.1 `Capabilities.ItemHandler.BLOCK` is one over
